# Crime types

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools refs render` from research/references/crime-types.yaml. Do not edit. -->

The crimes the police respond to. Scripts report one with `CrimeIsHappening` or
`SpawnCustomCrime`, set how many responders each type draws with `CfgCrimeResponders` and switch one with
`CfgEnableCrimeType`; the game reports others itself ([AI: crimes](../research/ai.md#crimes)).

!!! info "What is complete"

    All 15 types are listed. The names come from a table no code calls, so which name goes with
    which number is inferred from the types the code raises.

15 entries. Data: `research/references/crime-types.yaml`.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Hand-written | Meaning |

| `id` | int | | The crime type: `CrimeIsHappening`'s kind, `CfgCrimeResponders`' and `CfgEnableCrimeType`'s first argument. |
| `name` | str | | The name the executable's crime-name table gives it. |
| `response` | str | yes | What the game does when it is reported. |
| `responders` | list | | `CfgCrimeResponders` calls: `script: count`. |
| `enabled` | list | | `CfgEnableCrimeType` calls: `script: on/off`. |
| `reported` | int | | Script calls that report it (`CrimeIsHappening`, `SpawnCustomCrime`). |
| `scripts` | list | | The scripts that report it (at most six). |
| `source` | str | yes | Where the entry comes from: a script and binding, an address, a chunk. |

| `notes` | str | yes | Our own short notes. |
